faqs.q: How much does a doula cost in St. Petersburg?
faqs.a: Most Pinellas County doulas bill a flat package between $1,000 and $3,200, and the median lands near $2,000. Postpartum-only packages run $60 to $90 an hour. The Healthy Start Coalition of Pinellis runs a free doula program for county residents, so ‘how do we even afford one’ has a real answer now rather than a shrug. Start with the free birth plan and you'll know which pieces you actually want before you price them out.

faqs.q: Is there a birth center in St. Petersburg?
faqs.a: Closest to it: Breath of Life Women's Health & Birth Center in Largo is the only CABC-accredited birth center in the state, and it lists St. Petersburg among the areas its midwives cover. There's no in-city freestanding birth center on the Pinellas side yet, so most home-birth-oriented families pair a local doula with either a home birth or a hospital that honors the plan. If you're set on a center birth, Breath of Life is the one to call first.

faqs.q: Which St. Petersburg hospital should I use for the birth?
faqs.a: Two of them carry the most weight: Orlando Health Bayfront, which delivers into Johns Hopkins All Children's and has the strongest NICU adjacency, and HCA Florida St. Petersburg, a full-service hospital two minutes from downtown with private L&D rooms and midwife-attended births. Both take doulas as a support person. If it's your first birth and the risk picture is straightforward, either works; if you want the neonatal safety net closest, Bayfront is the one.

faqs.q: Does Florida Medicaid cover a doula?
faqs.a: Partially — Florida Medicaid covers doula services when they're part of an approved maternity-care plan, and the Healthy Start Coalition of Pinellas gives eligible county residents a doula at no cost for labor and the early postpartum period. If you're on Medicaid, the front doors are (727) 507-4260 for the coalition and your plan's maternity line for the covered-services route. Call both before your second trimester; the slots fill.

faqs.q: Can I bring my own doula to the hospital?
faqs.a: Yes, at both major hospitals — Bayfront and HCA Florida St. Petersburg each take one support person beyond the partner, and doulas count for that slot. Bring a signed birth plan, a photo ID, and the doula's cert paperwork; the admission desk will want all three before the L&D floor clears her in. The Leapfrog safety note at HCA explicitly nods to bringing your own doula, so there's no ‘staff doula only’ catch on the Pinellas side.
